findings.problem: The FilterCapabilities methods use different receiver types. IsEmpty has a pointer receiver and handles nil. SupportsLevel (line 153) and SupportsOperator (line 160) have value receivers. Callers reach these methods through SearchCapabilities.Filter, which is a *FilterCapabilities and is documented to be nil when the reader serves no filter. So caps.Filter.SupportsLevel(...) or caps.Filter.SupportsOperator(...) panics with a nil dereference in exactly the case the type documents as normal. The type doc says an empty FilterCapabilities means the same as a nil one, but only IsEmpty keeps that promise.
findings.fix: Change SupportsLevel and SupportsOperator to pointer receivers (c *FilterCapabilities) and make them nil-safe. SupportsLevel should return `level == "" || (c != nil && slices.Contains(c.Levels, level))`. SupportsOperator should return `c != nil && slices.Contains(c.Operators, op)`. All three methods then share one receiver type, and a nil *FilterCapabilities answers like the zero value.

findings.problem: TestFilterCapabilities_SupportsLevel and TestFilterCapabilities_SupportsOperator check only a populated value and the zero value. They never call the methods on a nil *FilterCapabilities, which is the case SearchCapabilities.Filter produces by default. TestFilterCapabilities_IsEmpty does cover nil, so the tests do not hold all three methods to the same nil-means-empty rule.
findings.fix: After the receiver change, add a `var none *FilterCapabilities` case to both tests. Assert that none.SupportsLevel("") is true, none.SupportsLevel(expression.LevelSpan) is false, and none.SupportsOperator(expression.OpAnd) is false, so that nil and the zero value are shown to answer the same.

kept.why: Confirmed at reader.go:147-161. IsEmpty uses a pointer receiver and handles nil, but SupportsLevel and SupportsOperator use value receivers. SearchCapabilities.Filter is a *FilterCapabilities and its doc says nil means 'none of it', so caps.Filter.SupportsLevel(...) panics with a nil dereference in that normal case. The type doc says an empty FilterCapabilities declares the same as a nil one, and these two methods break that. Nothing in this package calls them yet, but they are exported API meant for callers that hold the pointer. Switching to nil-safe pointer receivers fixes the panic and puts all three methods on one receiver type. This is a nil-safety bug, not one of the structural categories, so it is 'other'.
